key_insight: Among leading subquadratic sequence models, xLSTM performs best overall because its gating enables more flexible and stable memory correction and state tracking.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale sequence modeling, xLSTM is a strong alternative to quadratic attention when robust long-range dependency handling and better scalability are needed.
method: Compared xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet under a unified formulation.
Evaluated them on code pre-training, LLM-based code distillation, and time-series foundation model pre-training.
Used controlled synthetic length-generalization tasks to isolate memory and state-tracking behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that xLSTM achieves the strongest overall performance across the three application settings and is further supported by synthetic length-generalization experiments.
watch_item: The results are based on a focused benchmark set, so performance may vary on other sequence domains or under different training budgets and implementation details.
paper_title: On Subquadratic Architectures: From Applications to Principles
